Transformer shortage deepens as utilities race to expand grids

By Maria Keller

Lead times for large power transformers have stretched to between 120 and 210 weeks, according to procurement managers at three European utilities interviewed this month. The backlog reflects a surge in grid investment programmes and a limited supply of grain-oriented electrical steel.

Manufacturers say they are adding capacity, but new factories take years to commission. Hitachi Energy announced a further expansion of its transformer plant in Virginia, while Siemens Energy said demand for grid equipment remained at record levels.

Electrical steel is the bottleneck

Grain-oriented electrical steel is produced by a handful of mills worldwide. Procurement teams report that allocations for 2027 are already fully booked, and that spot prices have risen sharply over the past eighteen months.

Transformer classTypical lead time 2021Typical lead time 2026
Distribution12 weeks52 weeks
Large power50 weeks150 weeks

Utilities are responding by placing framework orders years ahead and by standardising designs so that units can be swapped between projects.
